nodes.description: Private mapping storing token balances for each address in ERC20.
Private nested mapping storing allowance owner=>spender=>amount in ERC20.
Private total token supply variable in ERC20.
Private owner address of Ownable, set at construction and changed on ownership transfer.
Public mint(address,uint256) restricted by onlyOwner; mints new tokens to a target address.
Internal ERC20 mint helper that increases _totalSupply and recipient balance.
Internal ERC20 transfer helper moving amount from sender to recipient.
Public ERC20 transfer that forwards msg.sender, recipient and amount to _transfer.
Public ERC20 transferFrom that moves tokens using allowance and reduces it via _approve.
Internal ERC20 helper writing the allowance mapping.
Address library sendValue which forwards ETH via a low-level call to an arbitrary payable recipient.
Ownable function guarded by onlyOwner that transfers ownership to newOwner.
Ownable function guarded by onlyOwner that sets _owner to the zero address.
Caller controlled msg.sender, exposed through Context._msgSender and used in access control checks.
Low-level external call recipient.call{value:amount}("") in Address.sendValue that transfers control to an untrusted address.
Parameter _to of mint, the address receiving newly minted tokens.
Parameter _amount of mint, the number of tokens to be minted.
Parameter recipient of transfer, the address receiving tokens.
Parameter amount of transfer, the number of tokens to move.
Parameter newOwner of transferOwnership, the address becoming the new owner.

edges.reason: mint is protected by the onlyOwner modifier, which compares _owner with _msgSender(); the caller controls whether the guarded body executes.
The owner state variable is read inside the onlyOwner modifier of mint to authorize the caller.
The _to parameter flows into mint and is forwarded to _mint as the token receiver.
The _amount parameter flows into mint and is forwarded to _mint as the mint amount.
mint invokes the internal _mint helper after the onlyOwner check passes.
_mint increases the _totalSupply state variable using SafeMath add.
_mint credits the newly created tokens to the _balances mapping entry of the recipient.
_transfer reads the sender and recipient balances from the _balances mapping before updating them.
_transfer writes the debited sender balance and the credited recipient balance back into _balances.
transfer passes _msgSender(), i.e. msg.sender, as the sender argument of _transfer.
The recipient parameter flows into transfer and onward to _transfer.
The amount parameter flows into transfer and onward to _transfer.
transfer calls the internal _transfer helper to perform the balance move.
transferFrom uses _msgSender() as the spender whose allowance is deducted, so the caller influences the authorization path.
transferFrom reads and reduces the caller allowance stored in the _allowances mapping.
transferFrom calls _transfer to move tokens from the sender to the recipient.
transferFrom calls _approve to write the reduced allowance after the transfer.
_approve writes the updated allowance amount into the _allowances mapping.
sendValue performs a low-level call forwarding all gas to an arbitrary payable recipient, handing control to untrusted code that could re-enter before state is finalized.
transferOwnership is guarded by onlyOwner, so msg.sender determines whether the ownership change executes.
transferOwnership reads _owner for the onlyOwner check and writes the new owner into it.
The newOwner parameter flows into transferOwnership and is stored into the _owner state variable.
renounceOwnership is restricted by onlyOwner, so the caller controls execution of the ownership renouncement.
renounceOwnership reads and then zeroes out the _owner state variable.

normalization_plan.reason: The _to argument exists only to be forwarded into _mint called by mint, so it should be normalized into the mint function node.
The _amount argument exists only to be forwarded into _mint called by mint, so it should be normalized into the mint function node.
The recipient argument is only consumed by transfer which forwards it to _transfer, so it should be merged into the transfer function node.
The amount argument is only consumed by transfer which forwards it to _transfer, so it should be merged into the transfer function node.
The newOwner argument is only used inside transferOwnership to update _owner, so it should be merged into the transferOwnership function node.
